title: Ibn Mas'ud aloud
hookLine: the small shepherd Abdullah ibn Mas'ud recites Surah ar-Rahman aloud at the Ka'ba and is beaten (sirah)

lines: WHO WILL MAKE THEM HEAR IT?
cards: A small circle of the Prophet's companions in Mecca, talking low. Ibn Ishaq gives their worry in a sentence: Quraysh have never heard this Qur'an recited openly to them. Who will make them hear it?

One voice answers: I will. It belongs to Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, a shepherd, slight and thin-legged, with no strong clan behind him. The others object; they want someone whose family will step in if the crowd turns on him.
He goes anyway. Today: Ibn Mas'ud.

teach.h: AT THE MAQAM, IN THE MORNING.
teach.b: The next morning, Ibn Ishaq says, he goes to the Ka'ba while the leaders of Quraysh sit in their meeting places, stands at the Maqam, and raises his voice.
He chooses the opening of surah fifty-five, ar-Rahman. In Pickthall's words: "The Beneficent Hath made known the Qur'an." Notice the choice.
Not a warning, not a threat.

A surah that opens with the name of mercy and lists gifts: the sun and moon, the sky raised up, the fruit and the palm, with a refrain that keeps coming back: "Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny?"
The crowd works out what he is reading, and they get up and strike him in the face.

teach.h: STRUCK IN THE FACE, STILL RECITING.
teach.b: He keeps reciting as far as he can, then goes back to his friends, his face marked. They say: this is what we were afraid of.
His answer, in Ibn Ishaq: God's enemies were never smaller in his eyes than now, and if they like, he'll do it again tomorrow. One more detail, from Musnad Ahmad.

teach.h: THIN LEGS, HEAVY ON THE SCALE.
teach.b: Once, some companions laughed at how thin Ibn Mas'ud's legs were, and the Prophet said those legs would weigh heavier on the scale than the mountain of Uhud.
Put the two together: the man some laughed at carried the words of mercy out loud, paid for it, and offered to go back.

how: Muslims recite the Qur'an aloud in prayer and in gatherings, and Ibn Mas'ud is remembered among the companions known for their recitation.

o: the call to prayer recited from the Ka'ba
a warning surah about the fate of Quraysh
the Beneficent, a name of God and Surah 55

practice: Choose a few lines that matter to you, a verse, a prayer you already know, a poem, a line your grandmother used to say, and say them in your full voice, slowly, so each word lands. If your voice shakes, let it shake.
Then sit quietly and notice how the room sounds after.

wordCard.voice: Ar-Rahman, the Beneficent: the surah Ibn Mas'ud chose to recite aloud at the Ka'ba, naming God's mercy before the crowd that beat him for it. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Most Merciful, the name that opens surah 55; Pickthall renders it "The Beneficent".

carryVoice: Your line: he recited it aloud. He chose words of mercy, and said them where it cost him. That's day seven hundred thirty-nine.
